payload.feature: brokkr export gains --redact: a sanitized copy for publishable fixtures. Today export writes the canonical NDJSON journal verbatim, and verbatim exports embed operator-machine detail — absolute paths and usernames in effect/started driver commands, checkpoint targets, and workdir fields (the review of the fold-arm slice recorded exactly this residual: the committed fixture is the one artifact in the public repo carrying [path-1]<user> paths). Scope: (1) 'brokkr export --run <id> --redact' writes, ALONGSIDE nothing else changed, a sanitized variant: every absolute filesystem path in event payload string fields is rewritten to a stable placeholder that preserves distinctness (the same original path always becomes the same placeholder, distinct paths stay distinct, e.g. [path-1], [path-2]), usernames inside such paths never survive, and everything else — event structure, seqs, hashes need not re-verify (see 3) — is untouched. (2) The redacted file and its manifest are UNMISTAKABLY marked as redacted (filename suffix and a manifest field), because a sanitized copy that could pass as verbatim evidence would be a forgery — decision 0019 law three's spirit applies to machines too. (3) Honesty about the chain: redaction breaks the recorded event hashes by construction; the redacted manifest must SAY so (a field naming the redaction and that hash verification applies only to the verbatim export), and 'brokkr export' WITHOUT --redact stays byte-identical to today. (4) Default output naming keeps the run id; --redact adds the marked suffix. Tests must pin: placeholder stability and distinctness; no username or absolute path survives anywhere in the redacted NDJSON; the redacted manifest carries the marking fields; the verbatim path is unchanged by the flag's existence; and a fixture-sized journal round-trips through redaction deterministically (same input, same output). CI enforces exact coverage — keep the gate green.

result.notes: Implemented marked deterministic redacted exports with stable distinct path placeholders while preserving verbatim export bytes; added proposed decision 0022 and fixture-sized coverage. cargo test --workspace, clippy, formatting, and exact coverage all pass.

cargo test --workspace: 552 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored across 31 test targets (all 'test result: ok', including the machine proof and differential corpus parity tests). cargo run -p forge-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self: compiled clean under the constitutional lint, digest 638a4efa2c4a425af0d709be626dfb5dcf0a84c6b1304de0bb830384f28ea29f, all five seats resolved with no notices.

Reviewed ef5c52d (export.rs + tests, --redact wiring in lib.rs, decision 0022). Correctness: sound. Placeholder table is journal-wide and insertion-ordered — stability, distinctness, and determinism hold; verbatim export byte-identity with the flag absent is pinned against store.export_ndjson output; the .redacted filename suffix and the three manifest marking fields (redacted, redaction, hash_verification) are all pinned; the test even pins verify_export FAILING on the redacted journal — the honesty clause proven, not just documented. Envelope fields outside payload are ids/timestamps/hashes (no path carriers), and the pinned run manifest holds only bundle-relative paths + digests, so scoping redaction to payload strings is correct. Both residuals the prior reviewer (15175f64) left on the discarded 1021dc4 incarnation are FIXED here: Windows drive-letter and UNC paths are recognized and tested; path ends are char-based so non-ASCII usernames redact fully (probe-verified). cargo test, clippy, fmt all green; deliver phase recorded exact coverage 11302/11302 lines, 1686/1686 branches, 987/987 functions. Simplicity: compact, idiomatic, no dead policy; decision 0022 fits the culture. FIXES APPLIED (f05a3f6, doc-only, no coverage surface): declared the two scanner bounds in export.rs rustdoc and 0022 consequences; README gains the --redact usage line it was missing. Adversarial probes (scratch, reverted) behaved safely on quoting, unclosed quotes, parens, newlines, PATH-style colon lists (over-redaction direction). RESIDUALS: (1) [low, security] file:///home/<user> URLs survive redaction — the :// scheme exclusion spares file:// URLs whose bodies ARE absolute local paths; no component journals such a URL today (recipes' file:// support is CLI-side bundle install, not journaled), so exposure needs a hand-written URL in a driver command; now a declared limitation, still unimplemented. (2) [info, security] a payload string already containing a literal [path-N] is indistinguishable from a genuine placeholder — an adversarial journal could seed these to confuse a fixture reader; cannot forge verbatim evidence since the derivative is marked and its hashes refuse verification; now documented. (3) [info] the fixture test's leak assertion reuses next_absolute_path, so it shares the scanner's blind spots (partially compensated by literal [path-1] and username contains-checks). (4) [info] ~<user>/ tilde paths keep usernames — outside the framed absolute-path scope. (5) [info] the motivating artifact fixtures/journals/tui-graph-*.ndjson still carries 27 [path-8] occurrences; re-exporting it needs the original DB and was not in this slice's scope — the feature now exists to burn it down. No finding at or above high — no security-hold.
